note:
Coverage. All 23 physical pages were read at text level and all 46 measured regions were inspected on a crop: p4, p6, p7, p8, p12 (twice), p13, p14 (twice), p15 (twice), p16, p18, p19 (twice) and p21. Table 3 on p15 was confirmed from a dedicated crop of the region-free half of the page, which is how the deficit below is established rather than inferred. 

The census arithmetic. Seventeen printed exhibits - thirteen charts and four grids - and sixteen of them measured. The loss is Table 3, the correlation coefficient grid on p15: six horizontal rules, no verticals, caption above, and no region anywhere near it. That is the fourth paper in a row to lose its cleanest table, and the mechanism is now beyond doubt: the clustering pass follows ink, and three thin rules are less ink than one word of prose. The 46 regions collapse to 17 exhibits only after 30 exclusions, and the exclusions are of two kinds: 25 fragments of figures the detector split (nineteen on p8, four on p7, two on p16 - the two p16 rasters are the same chart drawn twice inside its vector outline) and five pasted display equations (three on p6, one on p7, one on p19: the smoothing recurrences that Equation 22 numbers but does not print in the text layer). 

The split-figure convention, stated once. When one printed figure arrives as many regions, the recorded bbox is the largest fragment - the validator only accepts a measured region - but the recorded area_frac is the union of all the fragments, because the union is what the page actually shows. On p8 that is the difference between reporting 7.2 per cent and reporting 27.1 per cent of the page, and Fig.4 is the largest exhibit in the paper. Any aggregate built from area_frac on this paper is therefore an aggregate of drawn extent, not of region geometry; the README says which. 

Two numbering faults, both structural. First, order: Fig.11 prints on p16 and Fig.10 on p18, so the coupling model's fit arrives AFTER the comparison chart that is supposed to demonstrate the coupling, and the two backward pointers in the paper (Fig.5 read on p13 from p12, Fig.11 read on p17 from p16) are both consequences of the same habit of placing a figure where it is finished rather than where it is read. Second, naming: the paragraph that reads the piecewise index curve on p6 opens 'As the Fig.3 shows', so the curve is never named by its own number, and the sentence about Mexico's FCI on p17 calls the country Kenya. Four of the thirteen charts (Fig.1, Fig.2, Fig.12, Fig.13) are never named by number at all. 

Charts. No 3-D, no colourbar, no shared axes except where panels share a scale by accident (the four dendrograms of Fig.5 all use 0 to 4 and all carry the same dashed cut at 1.8, which is what defines the clusters, and no panel says so). Two families have no word in the vocabulary: Fig.5 is a dendrogram and Fig.4 is a radial mind map, filed as node-link-network as the nearest true description. The paper's most consistent habit is that every chart prints its axis numbers and almost none prints a title: Fig.6 has no axis titles at all, Fig.7 and Fig.8 have none on any of their five axes, and the two that do title their axes (Fig.10, Fig.12, Fig.13) do it properly with rotated titles. Legends are inside on three and absent on nine, and where a legend is absent the CAPTION does the keying - Fig.10 names its spline and its fit line, Fig.13 names its band. 

Tables. Three measured of four printed. Table 1 is three-rule booktabs split over the p4/p5 fold with no repeated header; Table 2 is the only fully boxed grid and the only one that merges cells, merging the group name down four rows while the group weight merges down the same four in another column; Table 4 is four thresholds in five columns, three rules, and it repeats Fig.6's printed critical values exactly, so the paper's tipping point exists twice in two formats and is reconciled in neither. No grid carries a unit in its header and none prints a unit outside its frame: the twelve indicators' units live only in the running prose on p8 to p10. 

Apparatus. The folio runs four pages behind the printed page ('Page 21 of 21' on p23 of 23) and the contents list claims 21 pages against 23 printed. A red Chinese resale banner prints across p6, p14 and p18 - two of them above exhibits, one of them directly above Fig.8's chart. Two phantom headings come from axis furniture: '28 Annual mean temperature' is Fig.8's top tick plus its legend key, and '52.0 FCI 30' is Fig.11's left tick, axis label and right tick, so the heading detector's rule (a left-margin number followed by words) interprets chart furniture as section numbers. The heading of 4.1.2 is typeset in a five-character column, so the text layer reads it as 'Extr eme weat her indi cato r' and the layout pass keeps only the first fragment.
rules: 23 physical pages carry 46 measured regions on 12 of them, and those 46 collapse to seventeen printed exhibits: thirteen charts (Fig.1 to Fig.13) and four grids (Table 1 to Table 4) [place.doc_order].

Table 3, the correlation-coefficient grid on p15, owns no region at all: it prints as six horizontal rules with no closed outline, so the clustering pass drops it - the fourth time in four papers that the cleanest table style is the one the detector cannot see [place.area_frac].

Twenty of the 46 regions are one infographic: the p8 mind map is twelve label rasters, five vector ellipses and three unlabelled rasters, so 43 per cent of this paper's measured regions belong to a single exhibit [place.area_frac].

For a figure the detector split, the recorded area is the union of its fragments, not the anchor region: Fig.4 stays at 0.271 of the page and Fig.3 at 0.104, against the 0.072 and 0.044 their largest fragments would report [place.area_frac].

Numbering is not print order: Fig.11 prints on p16 and Fig.10 two pages later on p18, so the paper's own sequence runs backwards and the coupling-model fit arrives after the comparison chart it explains [caption.numbering].

Every figure caption is the ABBREVIATED form with no space and no separator - 'Fig.1', 'Fig.2', ... 'Fig.13' - and every table caption is the bare form with no colon at all - 'Table 1 Notations', 'Table 4 Tipping point for each aspect' - which is neither of the two forms the vocabulary offers, 'Figure N' or 'Table N:' [caption.numbering].

Charts split line 4, bar 2, scatter 1, node-link-network 2, flowchart-or-schematic 1, composite-panel 2, heatmap-or-contour 1: there is no default chart type here, and two of the thirteen are mind maps or dendrograms the vocabulary has no word for [geometry.family].

Fig.5 is four dendrograms and Fig.4 is a radial mind map, both filed as node-link-network because the closed vocabulary has no dendrogram and no mind map - the same gap #164 hit with two treemaps [geometry.family].

Nothing in the paper is three-dimensional and nothing carries a colourbar; the only depth cues are gradient fills and drop shadows on the p4 and p8 diagrams, which are flat objects photographed with a shadow [geometry.three_d].

Legends run none 9, inside 3, below 1: the three inside keys are two bar charts (Fig.7, Fig.8) and one line chart (Fig.11), and the single key printed below the frame (Fig.6) keys a colour ramp [geometry.legend].

Two charts use the caption as their legend instead of a legend box - Fig.10 names its blue spline and its black dotted fit line, Fig.13 names its confidence band - so the caption is load-bearing wherever the legend is absent [geometry.legend].

Every chart prints numbers except three: Fig.1 and Fig.4 carry textual box labels and no scale at all, and Fig.3 prints only the symbols sigma, mu and 2 sigma, which is what separates a diagram from a chart in this paper [geometry.printed_numbers].
All thirteen figure captions print BELOW their object and all four table captions print ABOVE their grid - the cleanest caption-side discipline in the lane so far [caption.position].

Eight figure captions are bare noun phrases with no voice; three carry an active verb ('The index model has three subsections', 'The right part shows the increase', 'the model defines twelve indicators') and two are passive ('which is classified as', 'is made by the method of cubic spline') [caption.voice].

Captions run 3 to 40 words; the longest are the three that describe the drawing rather than name it - Fig.3 at 40, Fig.4 at 38, Fig.2 at 32 - and the shortest is the bare label plus noun of a grid caption ('Table 1 Notations', three words) [caption.words].

No caption states a unit, and the eight that name a variable name it as a symbol the caption cannot typeset - Fig.7 ends 'from FCI .' with the space its dropped equation glyph left behind [caption.verbatim].

Fig.9's caption keys its four panels '(a), (b), (c), (b)' - the fourth panel is lettered (d) on the drawing and keyed (b) in the caption, so one key is missing and one is used twice [caption.verbatim].

Fig.11's caption is seven words and its reading sentence names the wrong country: p17 says 'the FCI of Kenya rise up rapidly' inside a section titled 'Climate characteristics of Mexico' [caption.verbatim].

Grids split booktabs 2, boxed 1: the numbered body tables are three-rule booktabs, the one real data table (Table 2) is fully boxed with every internal rule drawn, and Table 3 - the grid that does not measure - is booktabs [table.rule_style].

No grid in the paper is zebra-striped; the shading that exists is categorical and carries meaning - cream for the fragility column, pale blue and peach for the two weight scales in Table 2 - which is the opposite of decorative banding [table.zebra].

Table 2 is the only grid that merges cells and it merges vertically in two columns at once, holding one group name over four indicator rows while the group weight is held over the same four [table.merged_cells].

Only Table 2 aligns its decimals, and it can because every one of its twelve weights prints to four places; Table 4's four thresholds print to two and would align if they had to [table.decimal_aligned].

No grid has a unit in its header row and no grid prints a unit outside its frame: the twelve indicators' units (kwh per capita, kg per hectare, per cent of GDP) are stated only in the running prose on p8 to p10 [table.units_in_header].
All three measured grids span the full measure (0.79 to 0.91 of the 438 pt text block) and all are portrait; the widest is Table 2 at 397 pt [table.width].
Table 1 is the paper's only continued grid: caption and header on p4, seven more rows on p5 with no repeated header, no 'continued' mark and no repeated caption [table.continued].

Twelve exhibits are pointed at by number - nine of the thirteen charts (Fig.3 to Fig.11) and all three measured grids - while Fig.1, Fig.2, Fig.12 and Fig.13 are never named by number anywhere [mention.first_page].

Two pointers run BACKWARD: Fig.5 is read on p13 although it prints on p12, and Fig.11 is read on p17 although it prints on p16 - so the paper's two backward references are both to the page it has just left [mention.lead_pages].

The pointer to Fig.2 names the wrong figure: the paragraph that reads the piecewise curve opens 'As the Fig.3 shows', so a reader following the number crosses the page turn to the schematic and never reaches the curve [mention.lead_pattern].

The pointer to Fig.4 is the only one that carries the finding before the number - 'As is vividly shown in Fig.4, in the context of global warming' - and it is the only figure introduced two pages ahead of its print [mention.lead_pattern].

Section kinds split result 7, model 6, test 1, sensitivity 1, symbols 1: every chart of a case study is filed under 'result' and the two construction diagrams under 'model', so the section a picture lives in predicts whether it shows a computed number [place.section_kind].
Zones run top 4, middle 6, bottom 6, and no exhibit owns a page to itself [place.page_zone].

Areas run mean 0.121, maximum 0.271 (Fig.4) and minimum 0.026 (Table 4, four thresholds in a two-row grid); every figure in the paper is at least 0.044 of its page (Fig.2), so nothing here is a fragment displayed as an exhibit [place.area_frac].

Two phantom headings come from axis furniture: '28 Annual mean temperature' on p14 is Fig.8's top tick plus its legend key, and '52.0 FCI 30' on p16 is Fig.11's left tick, its axis label and its right tick - the layout pass reads any left-margin number followed by words as a section number [place.section_path].

The document's folio runs four pages behind the printed page ('Page 21 of 21' on p23 of 23) and a red Chinese resale banner prints across p6, p14 and p18, two of them above exhibits [place.area_frac].

tables.note: The weights table, and the only grid in the paper that is a real data table read in both directions: five columns (Fragility / Indicators / Weights / Indicators / Weights), one header row, then twelve indicator rows grouped four economic, five ecosystem, three social - and the group name merged down its block in column 1 while the group weight is merged down the same block in column 3, so cells merge vertically in two columns at once (0.1145, 0.6055, 0.2800). Boxed: full outer frame plus every internal rule both ways, with the vertical rules in a paler grey than the horizontals. Shading is categorical, not zebra - the Fragility column is cream, the left Weights column pale blue, the right Weights column peach - so the two weight scales are told apart by colour rather than by a header the eye can hold. All twelve weights print to four decimal places and line up, the only decimal-aligned grid in the paper. The text layer cannot read it: values are emitted before the indicator names they belong to, so the extracted order runs 0.6055, 'Cereal yield', 0.1648.

tables.note: Four numbers and five words, the whole tipping-point definition: header 'Aspect / ERI / ESI / SHI / FCI', body 'Value / 71.25 / 62.15 / 59.49 / 63.29', three rules and no verticals, caption above. This is the paper's smallest exhibit by row count and its second smallest by area, and it duplicates Fig.6: those four numbers are exactly the fourth band's printed critical values one page-group earlier, so the paper states its definition once as a picture and once as a grid and never reconciles the two formats. It is also the only table whose every value is a threshold, and the only one where a decimal-aligned column is two characters wide.
